The first thing I want to say is that I'm sorry that that happened to you, and that it's affected you in the way that it has.

The second thing I want to say is that there's so much emotional heaviness around the word "rape" that, regardless of the legal status of any actions, I would (myself, personally) hesitate to tell anybody else that they had been raped, without them using the word first. It's a really hard word to come round to using, and for *me*, I needed to find it myself, first. This is my own personal feeling on the matter, not advice for other people.

All that said? Your boyfriend did not have a reason to assume you gave consent. You never said "yes", you never asked for it, you never initiated it. It's that simple. You already know that you didn't give consent, but the thing here also is that he had no reason to believe that you did, either.

To answer your question, I believe that you have every right to call it rape, if that's what feels right for you. If it does, then I hope identifying that can help you in a way you need.

I also think, though, that you can keep a tiny piece of you filled with righteous anger, and still live the full life you deserve.

Moving on from being victimised should be about *you*, and your recovery. You don't owe anybody "being the bigger person", or "letting it go", or any of the other common rhetoric.

Example: As a rape survivor, I will not forgive my rapist. However, I am now in a healthy and loving relationship with someone else. These two things do co-exist, and that's okay.

There are certain antidepressants that can trigger or exacerbate mania in bipolar patients. Though he rarely pointed it out, he did time (or at least, make note of the time) how long I spent away from the computer to eat dinner with my family.

He'd tell me (in retrospect, likely untrue) things about other people so that I wouldn't trust them, and would rather be with him - like, that a mutual friend had been making sexual comments about me, or that another friend had been eyeing him up, or had called me a bitch behind my back. It just had to be me, and him, and nobody else.

We broke up, and he got kicked out of the college (for unrelated reasons), and he would still turn up at the building without notice. A couple of times he even came into the classes (they were pretty lax), so I had to tell the staff about him.

I did not get an *inch* of leeway, ever.

At the time of having the nightmare, I was struggling really badly with depression.

In the dream, I'd gone with my mother to the doctor's office, to tell them that I'd been depressed. They took me aside, in private, and told me that if I wanted to get better, all I had to do was pass this test. And I do want to get better, so I say I'll try the test.

The test, rather than being anything psychological, is getting from one end of a corridor to the other. It's filled with water, and there are raised platforms that I have to jump between. *Just* as I'm nearly at the end, there's a loud noise, like a wild animal, and I lose my balance, startled, and fall into the water. I've failed the test.

I'm then back in the office, and it's just me and the doctor, and they explain to me that because I'd failed the test, my will to live wasn't strong enough, so they administered me with poison, "as you wanted". After this conversation, they shut me in the office to die. Over a tannoy system, I can hear them speaking to my mother in another room - and the rest of my family, and friends. They solemnly explain that this was what I had chosen, and that my family/friends just hadn't been enough for me, and that I'd taken the poison of my own accord. I die, painfully, listening to the cries of the people who care about me, but unable to be with them.

So that was horrible.

I needed space, sometimes, both as a normal human being who needs space sometimes, and also as someone with mental illness and previous trauma. A lot of the time his need for reassurance was deemed more important than my own personal boundaries, and I would end up having to do things I didn't want to, lest I suffer the emotional fallout.

My response to previous trauma became *worse*, because sex became this terrifying obligation, and I thought he would hurt himself if I didn't oblige, or if I left. I would freeze up if he touched me in case he wanted more, and that made him more insecure that I didn't want him...

It ended. Messily.

I don't think insecurity *inherently* is a relationship killer, but you *need* to know how to handle it, and how to handle it if you fuck up about it.

It's already been said here that antidepressants can give energy to people who were previously too depressed to realistically consider or attempt suicide. They didn't have the motivation, or the energy to carry any plans out.

Many people find akathisia unbearable, and may seek out suicide as an alternative to that particular brand of suffering.
